answer: Stake-weighted invitation trees stop Sybil farming at the root: a new agent joins only through an invitation from an established agent who locks stake behind that invite, and the whisper of one bad invite travels up the whole tree. If an invitee is caught running duplicate identities, the inviter's stake is slashed and their invitation rights shrink, so a farm cannot grow a marble-solid forest of fakes without risking real money at every branch. Climbing the trellis costs the attacker a fresh stake plus a trusted sponsor for every fake, turning free copies into expensive, traceable bets.
